text:
mira: Heads up — our eval CI started failing on metric_aggregation for quantized model bring-ups. Seeing negative pass@k values in the dashboard and weird BERTScore NaNs. Anyone hit this today? :eyes:

conor: I noticed the job `eval/runner/249` flaked earlier. CI link: https://ci.redwood.internal/ev/249 — logs show pass@k = -0.02 in the summary. That can't be right.

mira: Pasted the aggregator snippet here, minimal repro in local runner:```python
def compute_pass_at_k(success_counts, n, k):
    # success_counts: array of number of successful samples per example
    return success_counts.sum() / comb(n, k)  # ???
```
Seems suspect — comb(n,k) in denominator doesn't make sense for our sampled-top-k estimator.

alejandra: Yup that's the bug. We accidentally switched from the Monte-Carlo passthrough estimator to a combinatorics formula used for exact pass@k under i.i.d. sampling. For sampled outputs we should be using the usual unbiased estimator:```python
# recommended: for each example with c successes among n samples
# pass@k_est = 1 - comb(n-c, k)/comb(n, k)
# implemented with logs to avoid overflow when n large
```
Also the current implementation does integer division in some places which produced negatives after underflow with dtype=int32.

sam: Another wrinkle — BERTScore NaNs came from tokenization mismatch between our detokenize() step and the BERTScore library. The pipeline normalized punctuation in the reference but not in generated candidates; scorer returned zero-length embeddings for some cases. Quick fix: apply the same normalize function to both sides before passing to bert_score.score().

conor: CI flakiness root cause: our test harness samples `n=16` outputs and relies on RNG state from the model container. Quantized runtimes used a different PRNG implementation so sample order changed -> c values differ -> pass@k fluctuates. Repro: set seed in runner and use numpy.random.default_rng(42) to get deterministic draws across platforms.

mira: Good catch. So immediate action list? I can open a PR with: 1) fix pass@k formula + unit tests, 2) enforce int64 & float64 for aggregator math, 3) normalization wrapper for BERTScore, 4) add deterministic RNG seeding in CI harness. Anything else?

alejandra: Add invariants to unit tests: pass@k in [0,1], monotonicity w.r.t k (pass@k should not decrease when k increases), and small-scale analytic checks (n=3 table of values). For calibration metric, also add a sanity check: reliability bins should sum to number of examples. We had a bug where 0/1 labels were flipped when computing predicted_vs_actual, which is why our calibration curves looked underconfident.

sam: Dashboard note — reporting pipeline currently rounds BERTScore to 2 decimal places in the UI; that made NaNs show up as `-` but pass@k negative values made it into alerts. Suggest we clamp reported metrics to [0,1] before alerting and add an internal `raw_metrics` table for debugging.

eval-bot: CI job failed: eval/runner/249 — failing tests: metrics.test_passatk_bounds, metrics.test_bert_tokenization_consistency. Link: https://ci.redwood.internal/ev/249/logs

conor: I'll draft the pass@k PR and include the analytic unit tests. @mira can you handle the BERTScore tokenization wrapper and dashboard clamping? I'll also add a test that runs quantized runtime in a deterministic mode.

mira: Yep, grabbing the tasks. I'll also patch the calibration mapping bug (flipped labels). Will ping when PRs are up. :thumbsup:

sam: Thanks team. Once PRs land, let's add a short postmortem blurb in #eng-ml summarizing the root causes so oncall sees the checklist for future brings.

alejandra: Agreed. Small follow-up: consider adding a lightweight eval-lint that validates metric invariants on PRs to catch these before merge.

mira: +1 to eval-lint. Opening follow-up issue after fixes.

conor: Nice. Dropping a quick patch branch now: `fix/metrics-passatk-seed` — pushing tests.

mira: Thanks — I'll monitor the CI.
